# Tidy Tuesday

## Penguin Data

```{r, message = F}
### Import data set
many_penguins <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-07-14/many_penguins.csv')

# Load library
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r, warning = FALSE, message = F}

### Wrangle data for iceberg 
dat0 <- many_penguins

dat1 <- dat0 |>
  # Subset to relevant vars
  dplyr::select(shortname, contains("length")) |> 
  # Pivot to long format for fill
  pivot_longer(-shortname, names_to = "feature", values_to = "length") |>
  ### Keep complete cases
  drop_na() |>
  ### Filter out cases that distort the visual 
  filter(length < 41 & length > 10) |>
  ### Drop irrelevant var
  select(-feature)

### Create data for penguin 
temp_dat <- data.frame(shortname =
                        c("T", "W", "T", "T", "T", # first column
                          "X", "Y", "U", "U", "U", # second column
                          "W", "V", "V", "V", "T"), # third column
                      length = c(rep(6, 5), # first column
                                 7, 7, NA, 7, 7, # second column
                                 rep(8, 5))) # third column

last_row <- data.frame(shortname = "Y", length = 7)

### Combine real and fake penguin data
dat2 <- bind_rows(dat1, temp_dat, last_row) 

dat3 <- dat2 |>
  ### Remove cells that create a weird spike in iceberg 
  filter(!(grepl("E.", shortname) & round(length, 0)==36))

#### Set up colors for fill - gradient for real penguin data, specific colors for fake penguin data
fill_list <- c(scales::seq_gradient_pal(
  "white", "#a3b9f7", "Lab")(seq(0, 1, length.out = 16)),
        "#000000", "#000000", "#000000",
        "orange", "#f5d89f", "white")

### Make the plot!
dat3 |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = length, fill = shortname)) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#497fe3")) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = fill_list) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 25))
```
